extracted.intended_audience: practitioners (patent attorneys/agents) and lawyers advising clients before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Official professional conduct rules and ethical standards (comparative ABA Model Rules and USPTO Rules) governing practitioners who represent clients before the USPTO, covering conflicts, client relationships, client property, recordkeeping, and termination of representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement of malpractice claims with unrepresented client
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not settle a claim or potential claim for malpractice liability with an unrepresented client or former client unless that person is advised in writing of the desirability of seeking and is given a reasonable opportunity to seek the advice of independent legal counsel in connection therewith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written advice to the unrepresented client about seeking independent counsel and providing a reasonable opportunity to obtain such advice are mandatory prerequisites to settlement; protects against coercive releases by practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on acquiring proprietary interest in client's cause of action
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not acquire a proprietary interest in the cause of action, subject matter of litigation, or a proceeding before the Office which the practitioner is conducting for a client, except as provided in the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted exceptions: (1) acquire a lien authorized by law to secure fees or expenses; (2) contract for a reasonable contingent fee in a civil case; (3) in a patent case or proceeding before the Office, take an interest in the patent or patent application as part or all of the fee. Any such exceptions are 'subject to the other provisions in this section.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual relations with a client
rubrics_metrics.description: ABA: A lawyer shall not have sexual relations with a client unless a consensual sexual relationship existed when the client-lawyer relationship commenced. USPTO: (j) [Reserved].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under ABA rule the prohibition is absolute unless pre-existing consensual relationship; USPTO leaves this paragraph reserved (no active rule text in this section of the USPTO Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties to former clients — adverse representation prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who has formerly represented a client in a matter shall not thereafter represent another person in the same or a substantially related matter in which that person’s interests are materially adverse to the interests of the former client unless the former client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where matters are the same or substantially related and where interests are materially adverse; informed consent must be confirmed in writing. Mirrors ABA Rule 1.9/§11.109.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties to former clients — confidentiality and information use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who formerly represented a client shall not use information relating to the representation to the disadvantage of the former client, nor reveal information relating to the representation, except as the USPTO Rules would permit or when the information has become generally known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References USPTO_RULES §§ 11.106 and 11.109(c) (analogs to ABA Rules 1.6/1.9). The prohibition on use/revelation extends to information acquired during prior representation that is material to the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputation of conflicts — general rule for firms
rubrics_metrics.description: While practitioners are associated in a firm, none of them shall knowingly represent a client when any one of them practicing alone would be prohibited from doing so by the conflict rules, unless specified exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: (1) the prohibition is based on a personal interest of the disqualified practitioner and does not present a significant risk of materially limiting representation by remaining practitioners; or (2) the prohibition arises from association with a prior firm (Rule 1.9(a)/(b)) and the disqualified practitioner is timely screened, apportioned no fee, prompt written notice given to affected former client describing screening and compliance, and agreement to respond to inquiries. Certifications of compliance may be required at reasonable intervals upon former client's request and on termination of screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm representation after a lawyer/practitioner leaves
rubrics_metrics.description: When a practitioner has terminated association with a firm, the firm is not prohibited from representing a person with interests materially adverse to those of a client represented by the formerly associated practitioner, unless the matter is same or substantially related and any practitioner remaining in the firm has material information protected by the confidentiality rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the remaining practitioners possess material confidential information protected under §§ 11.106 and 11.109(c), representation is barred unless the affected client gives informed consent in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver and relation to other rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A disqualification prescribed by the imputation rule may be waived by the affected client under the conditions stated in the conflict-of-interest waiver provision (Rule 1.7/§11.107). The disqualification of practitioners associated with former or current government lawyers is governed by the government employee conflict rule (Rule 1.11/§11.111).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references for waiver mechanics and special government-employee imputation guidance; practitioners must follow the separate procedures when government affiliations are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special conflicts for former or current government employees
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is a former or current Federal government employee shall not engage in conduct contrary to applicable Federal ethics law; shall not represent a client in connection with a matter in which the practitioner participated personally and substantially as a public officer or employee unless the appropriate government agency gives informed consent confirmed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disqualified under this rule, the practitioner must be screened and the appropriate government agency must be given written notice to ascertain compliance. Confidential government information obtained while a government employee (defined as information obtained under governmental authority that the government is prohibited or privileged from disclosing and not otherwise public) may not be used to the material disadvantage of a person; a firm may represent only if the disqualified practitioner is timely screened and apportioned no fee. Current public officers/employees are subject to Rules 1.7/1.9 and must not participate in matters they previously handled, nor negotiate for private employment with persons involved in matters they are personally and substantially participating in (with narrow clerk exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Former judge, arbitrator, mediator or other third-party neutral conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not represent anyone in a matter in which the practitioner participated personally and substantially as a judge, adjudicative officer, law clerk, arbitrator, mediator, or other third-party neutral, unless all parties to the proceeding give informed consent confirmed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disqualified, no other practitioner in the firm may undertake the representation unless the disqualified practitioner is timely screened, apportioned no part of the fee, and written notice is promptly given to the parties and any appropriate tribunal so they can ascertain compliance. An arbitrator chosen as a partisan on a multi-member panel is not prohibited from subsequently representing that party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization as client — identity and reporting up
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner employed or retained by an organization represents the organization acting through its duly authorized constituents. If a practitioner knows that an associated person is engaged in action, intends to act, or refuses to act in a matter related to the representation that violates a legal obligation to the organization or violates law that could be imputed to the organization and is likely to result in substantial injury, the practitioner shall proceed as reasonably necessary in the best interest of the organization, including referring the matter to higher authority within the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner should, unless reasonably believing otherwise, refer the matter to the highest authority that can act on behalf of the organization. If the highest authority fails to address the violation and it is reasonably certain to result in substantial injury, the practitioner may reveal information relating to the representation to the extent reasonably necessary to prevent substantial injury (even if confidentiality rules would otherwise prohibit disclosure), subject to specified exceptions (e.g., investigations or defense related to alleged violations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization as client — explaining identity and dual representation
rubrics_metrics.description: When dealing with an organization’s directors, officers, employees, members, shareholders, or other constituents, a practitioner shall explain the identity of the client when the practitioner knows or reasonably should know that the organization’s interests are adverse to those of the constituents with whom the practitioner is dealing. A practitioner representing an organization may also represent its constituents, subject to the conflict rules (§ 11.107); required consent must be given by an appropriate official other than the individual who is to be represented (or by shareholders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires clarity about who the 'client' is and appropriate authorization/consent when there is dual representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client with diminished capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: When a client’s capacity to make adequately considered decisions is diminished (minority, mental impairment, or other reasons), the practitioner shall, as far as reasonably possible, maintain a normal client-practitioner relationship. When the practitioner reasonably believes the client is at risk of substantial physical, financial or other harm and cannot adequately act in their own interest, the practitioner may take reasonably necessary protective action, including consulting with persons who can protect the client and, in appropriate cases, seeking appointment of a guardian ad litem, conservator, or guardian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information relating to the representation of a client with diminished capacity is protected by confidentiality rules (§ 11.106). When taking protective action, the practitioner is impliedly authorized to reveal information to the extent reasonably necessary to protect the client's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safekeeping property — separation and record preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall hold property of clients or third persons that is in the practitioner's possession in connection with a representation separate from the practitioner's own property. Funds shall be kept in a separate account maintained in the state where the practitioner’s office is situated (or elsewhere with client consent). Other property shall be identified and appropriately safeguarded. Complete records of such account funds and other property shall be kept and preserved for a period of five years after termination of the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On receiving funds/property in which a client/third person has an interest, the practitioner shall promptly notify that person, promptly deliver any funds/property they are entitled to receive, and, upon request, render a full accounting. When property is claimed by two or more persons, keep property separate until dispute resolved and promptly distribute undisputed portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client trust account handling — deposits and withdrawals
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may deposit the practitioner's own funds in a client trust account only for bank service charges in an amount necessary for that purpose. Fees and expenses paid in advance must be deposited into a client trust account and withdrawn only as fees are earned or expenses incurred. Withdrawals shall be made only by check payable to a named payee (not to cash) or by authorized electronic transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that advance fees are not commingled and are only drawn down as earned; restricts cash withdrawals to avoid misappropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client trust account recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must maintain current financial records and retain specified records for five years after termination of representation, including: receipt and disbursement journals (identifying date, source, description of deposits and details of disbursements); ledger records for each client/beneficiary showing source and disposition of funds; copies of retainer/compensation agreements; copies of accountings to clients/third persons; copies of bills for fees and expenses; records showing disbursements on behalf of clients; physical/electronic equivalents of checkbook registers, bank statements, cancelled checks; records of electronic transfers (authorizer, date, recipient, confirmations); copies of monthly trial balances and quarterly reconciliations; and copies of client file portions reasonably related to trust account transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records may be maintained electronically provided printed copies can be produced and records are readily accessible. Compliance may be met by satisfying state recordkeeping requirements where the practitioner is licensed or where principal place of business is located, or by complying with the rule's requirements. Special provisions for law firms employing patent agents/limited-recognition persons to meet at least one practitioner's state requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client trust account safeguards — authorized signatories and deposit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a practitioner or a person under the direct supervision of the practitioner shall be an authorized signatory or authorize transfers from a client trust account. Receipts shall be deposited intact and records of deposit should be sufficiently detailed to identify each item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts who can access/authorize trust account transfers; requires detailed deposit records and intact deposits to ensure accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and form of trust account records
rubrics_metrics.description: Records required by the trust account rules may be maintained by electronic, photographic, or other media provided they otherwise comply with the rules and printed copies can be produced. Records shall be readily accessible to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows modern recordkeeping formats but mandates accessibility and producibility. Records kept by a lawyer/practitioner are deemed compliant if they meet applicable state requirements as an alternative compliance route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declining or terminating representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as stated in paragraph (c), a practitioner shall not represent a client or, if representation has commenced, shall withdraw from representation if: (1) the representation will result in violation of the Rules of Professional Conduct or other law; (2) the practitioner's physical or mental condition materially impairs the practitioner's ability to represent the client; (additional grounds may appear in subsequent paragraphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early paragraphs set mandatory withdrawal obligations to prevent unlawful or incompetent representation; other subsections (not fully shown in this chunk) contain permissive withdrawal circumstances and procedural requirements.
